description: Rice disease treatment knowledge base. Class names must match training image folder names exactly.

bacterial_leaf_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked to yellowish stripe on leaf margins, later turning white to gray. Leaves wilt and roll. In severe cases entire plant wilts (kresek stage).
bacterial_leaf_blight.favorable_conditions: High humidity, heavy rainfall, high nitrogen, temperatures 25-34 degrees C, strong winds.

treatment.chemical: Spray Copper Oxychloride (3g/L) or Streptocycline (0.5g/L) + Copper Sulphate (2.5g/L). Repeat after 10-14 days if needed.
treatment.organic: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens bioagent (10g/L) as foliar spray. Avoid excess nitrogen top-dressing.
treatment.systemic: Drain the field and stop nitrogen fertilizer application immediately when infection is detected.

bacterial_leaf_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties (IR64, Swarna Sub-1). Treat seeds with Streptocycline before sowing. Avoid high nitrogen doses. Ensure proper field drainage. Remove and burn infected stubbles.

brown_spot.symptoms: Circular to oval brown spots with yellow halo on leaves. Spots have dark brown border. Grains also infected causing grain discoloration and reduced quality.
brown_spot.favorable_conditions: Nutrient-deficient soils especially low potassium and silicon, drought stress, temperatures 25-30 degrees C, high humidity.

treatment.chemical: Spray Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Propiconazole (1ml/L) or Iprodione (2ml/L). Apply 2 sprays at 10-day interval.
treatment.organic: Improve soil fertility first. Apply potassium fertilizer. Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens.
treatment.systemic: Correct soil nutrient deficiencies. This disease is strongly linked to poor soil nutrition especially potassium deficiency.

brown_spot.prevention: Use well-fertilized soil with balanced NPK. Potassium top-dressing reduces severity significantly. Use certified seeds. Seed treatment with Mancozeb (3g/kg).

leaf_blast.symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions with gray center and brown border on leaves. Lesions have yellow halo. Severe infection causes entire leaves to dry up.
leaf_blast.favorable_conditions: Cool nights below 20 degrees C, high humidity, heavy dew, temperatures 20-28 degrees C, excess nitrogen.

treatment.chemical: Spray Tricyclazole (0.6g/L) or Isoprothiolane (1.5ml/L) or Azoxystrobin (1ml/L). Apply immediately at first sign. Repeat after 10 days.
treatment.organic: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L). Silicon-based foliar spray strengthens cell walls.
treatment.systemic: Reduce nitrogen top-dressing. Avoid excess irrigation.

leaf_blast.prevention: Use blast-resistant varieties. Seed treatment with Tricyclazole (2g/kg seed). Balanced nitrogen application. Avoid dense planting. Monitor field regularly from tillering stage.

panicle_blast.symptoms: Brown to black lesion at the base of panicle neck node. Infected panicles turn white and remain unfilled with empty grains. Entire panicle may break and fall.
panicle_blast.favorable_conditions: Same as leaf blast. Most damaging at flowering and grain filling stage.

treatment.chemical: Spray Tricyclazole (0.6g/L) or Propiconazole (1ml/L) at boot stage before heading and again at 50% heading. This is the critical application window.
treatment.organic: Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens at boot leaf stage. Silicon supplementation reduces severity.
treatment.systemic: Cannot undo damage once neck is infected. Preventive spray is essential.

panicle_blast.prevention: Preventive fungicide spray at boot stage is the single most important control measure. Use resistant varieties. Balanced fertilization. Do not apply heavy nitrogen at heading stage.

narrow_brown_spot.symptoms: Narrow, linear brown spots running parallel to leaf veins. Spots are dark brown with no distinct halo unlike regular brown spot. Lesions are narrow and elongated giving a streaked appearance.
narrow_brown_spot.favorable_conditions: High humidity, temperatures 25-30 degrees C, dense planting, nutrient deficient soils.

treatment.chemical: Spray Mancozeb (2.5g/L) or Carbendazim (1g/L) or Propiconazole (1ml/L). Apply 2 sprays at 10-day interval when symptoms first appear.
treatment.organic: Improve soil potassium levels. Spray Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L). Remove and destroy infected leaves.
treatment.systemic: Correct soil nutrient deficiency. Improve field drainage and reduce humidity through proper plant spacing.

narrow_brown_spot.prevention: Balanced NPK fertilization especially adequate potassium. Avoid dense planting. Use certified disease-free seeds. Seed treatment with Mancozeb (3g/kg). Crop rotation.

healthy.symptoms: No visible disease symptoms. Leaves are green and healthy.
healthy.prevention: Continue current practices. Monitor weekly for early signs of disease.
